input.quote: IBM may cancel any and all Purchase Orders against this Agreement at any time. In the event IBM cancels Purchase Order as the result of MSL's default, no cancellation charge shall be applicable. IBM's termination of Purchase Orders for its convenience shall not relieve IBM of any cost reimbursements under the Price section.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay obligation, shortfall penalty or volume cap on IBM. Purchases arise only under Purchase Orders (§6.0, p0720: "This Agreement does not authorize MSL to produce or deliver any Product"), and IBM may cancel any and all Purchase Orders at any time (§6.1, p0722), so fees are payable only for ordered Products — the preferred position. MSL bears inventory ownership and IBM expressly has "no liability for inventories that MSL purchases" where forecast accuracy is met (p0903) and "no liability for unused flexibility" under the Supply Flexibility Appendix (p0927). Two residual, non-material points noted rather than flagged: (i) if Requirements Accuracy falls below the stated threshold, IBM compensates MSL by a formula applied to material cost of shipped volume (Appendix 2, p1189-p1191) — a true-up on forecast error, not a volume commitment or penalty; and (ii) on termination for default IBM may be required to buy Parts inventory and on-order Parts against its forecasts, but only within the Appendix 4 Supply Flexibility parameters and excluding cancelable/transferable Parts (p0132-p0135, p0143), with an exit available via §4.0 (six months' notice at renewal). No redline proposed.
